Subject: Discount waterfall execution playbook — pricing exhibit redlines

Rishi,

Thanks for taking this on. We reviewed the redline your legal team sent on Exhibit B (pricing schedule). A couple of things we want to get aligned on before we re-file: 

- The discount waterfall (Section 3.2) currently ties step-downs to monthly committed units. We need to confirm how this maps to Redwood's token/embedding unit definitions so our billing team avoids double-counting.
- The proposed "stabilization surcharge" cap (max 6% of monthly bill) is OK in principle, but we need an ops playbook that explains when that surcharge is applied and how it de-escalates over the first 90 days.
- We asked procurement to flag the early-exit true-up mechanics — specifically the floor protection for the first 12 months. Can you provide an execution runbook we can show Finance?

If you can attach a short operational playbook and a clean redline (one that highlights only the pricing exhibit and the billing mapping sheet), that would help speed internal approval.

Best,
Sam Harris
Director, Procurement
Bluepine Health

Attachment: pricing_requirements_summary.pdf (summary of their billing questions)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Harris <sam.harris@bluepine.io>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discount waterfall execution playbook — pricing exhibit redlines

Sam —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've looped in Neha (billing ops) and Jordan (legal/programs). Attached are three items: a focused redline on Exhibit B ("20261213_Redline_v2.docx"), a 2-page execution playbook that describes surcharge triggers and de-escalation windows ("pricing_execution_playbook_v1.pdf"), and an exportable billing-metric mapping CSV that maps our internal units to the schedule line items ("billing_metric_mapping.csv").

High-level answers up front: 
1) Unit mapping: the waterfall steps map to "billable_units" in the CSV. For text gen tokens we treat "generation tokens" and "prompt tokens" separately and map to the same Exhibit B line via a single conversion multiplier. The CSV includes examples for a 10k, 100k, and 1M token month.
2) Stabilization surcharge: applied only when monthly actuals exceed forecast by >35% and sustained for 2 consecutive billing cycles. The surcharge phases down 50% after the second month of remediation and is removed after 90 days if utilization normalizes. Cap at 6% of the monthly invoice (as proposed).
3) Early-exit/floor protection: the redline retains the 12-month floor but adds a true-up matrix tied to realized run-rate across the first 4 quarters to avoid cliff reconciliations.

A couple of asks from our side to make the playbook operational for Finance/Procurement: 
- Can you confirm which internal Bluepine billing email (procurement@bluepine.io or billing@bluepine.io) will receive the monthly surcharge notices?
- We recommend you accept the redline with our operational annex and then we can switch to a canary-run for the first quarter (notification + one-month grace) to validate the metric mapping.

If that works I can get Jordan to prepare the final mark for signature and Neha will supply the sample invoice lines you can use to reconcile.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Director, Sales 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20261213_Redline_v2.docx (clean redline focused on Exhibit B); pricing_execution_playbook_v1.pdf; billing_metric_mapping.csv

Rishi/Neha —

Thanks for the fast turn. A couple clarifications from Finance: 
1) The CSV mapping looks good but we need a deterministic example that shows how a monthly blended rate is computed when the client runs two models (gen-heavy + embed-heavy) in the same billing month. Can you add an example row where both model types appear and show the waterfall step applied?
2) For the surcharge trigger, Finance asks that we add an explicit "forecast correction" path — i.e., if the customer provides updated forecast within the first 30 days of the overage window, the surcharge calculation should treat the updated forecast as the baseline for de-escalation.
3) Regarding notification: procurement@bluepine.io will receive the notice; billing@bluepine.io will receive the invoice. Please ensure the playbook lists both emails and the required attachments (sample invoice + itemized delta).

We are open to the suggested canary-run. Please include the deterministic blended-rate example and update the playbook to show the forecast correction flow. Once we have those edits we'll route the package to Legal for final sign-off.

Regards,
Bluepine Procurement Team

Bluepine procurement team —

Thanks for the notes. We updated the playbook to include a deterministic blended-rate example (row added to billing_metric_mapping.csv) showing gen + embed usage in the same month and the waterfall step computation. We also added a short section called "Forecast Correction" that: 
- Allows Bluepine to submit an updated forecast within the first 30 days following the first overage notice;
- Specifies that the updated forecast becomes the baseline for de-escalation calculations only if accompanied by a short justification (one paragraph) and the updated forecast is accepted by Redwood Finance.

Operational next steps we propose: 
1) Bluepine accepts the redline and operational annex (we'll prepare a single consolidated mark).
2) Execute a 90-day canary with one-month notification + one-month grace for the first billing cycle where the surcharge would apply.
3) If canary validates mapping, surcharge triggers and forecast correction work as expected, the standard Exhibit B language takes effect for month 4 onward.

Jordan will perform a legal pass on the final consolidated mark and route to DocuSign. If Bluepine is good with that timeline, I'll add the acceptance milestone to the HubSpot deal.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Manager, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
